metric_note: TNB Green Lane Pathway for data centres taking 132/275kV supply: implementation period cut 'from 36-48 months to just 12 months' (launched 8 Aug 2023). Petromindo (Aug 2026) cites TNB energising a Sedenak campus in 12 months as an example.
Normal delivery time for high-voltage data centre supply before the Green Lane, per the same TNB release.

Allocation only, no open grid queue. Pause on new data centres from 2019, lifted Jan 2022; capacity is then awarded through DC-CFA rounds (about 80MW in Jul 2023; 200MW in Aug 2026, all on Jurong Island). Agencies will review need for another round in 18 to 24 months.

Dominion said in Aug 2024 that connecting large data centres would take 1 to 3 years longer than the prior 3 to 4 years, so roughly 4 to 7 years. JLL 2026 outlook (via Construction Owners Club) puts a 100MW connection at about 7 years.
source_name: Bloomberg via Data Center Knowledge, 30 Aug 2024

metric_note: Consultancy estimate: a 500MW transmission-level campus takes 4 to 6 years from application to full power under current conditions; ERCOT large-load queue about 410GW (Apr 2026). Knight Frank Atlas 2026: some DFW projects pushed more than 12 months past target dates.
Qualitative: Ember describes a de facto moratorium on new Dublin data centres until 2028 (EirGrid constraint); no months-to-power figure published.
source_name: Ember, Grids for data centres in Europe, 19 Jun 2025

metric_note: Statista chart of average grid connection lead time for data centres in 2025 lists Amsterdam at 10 years (with Tokyo, the longest). Slaughter and May: connection times in severely congested Dutch areas reach up to ten years. Amsterdam also had a one-year moratorium from 2019.

Derived: Mainova (Mar 2026) says large high-capacity new connections can only be provided again from the mid-2030s, roughly 8 to 10 years out. Ember: European primary markets average 7 to 10 years, up to 13.

Knight Frank: securing new connections in core West London availability zones can take 5 to 10+ years. In 2022 the GLA warned three West London boroughs of grid limits to 2035, blaming data centre load.
Up to 10 years: Knight Frank cites TEPCO that the wait for new power connections in inner Tokyo now stretches up to 10 years; Statista 2025 chart also gives Tokyo 10 years.

Derived: Transgrid position (Sep 2026) that existing Sydney capacity is largely committed and no further capacity will be available until Sydney Ring South is completed in the mid 2030s, roughly 8 to 10 years out.
Proxy only: Maharashtra energy secretary says a proposed 765kV substation for the data centre cluster could take 3 to 5 years; land request pending about 18 months. Not a connection-queue figure.

Qualitative: no published PLN months-to-power figure found. Industry reports permitting of 6 to 9 months and unfinished transmission (Petromindo, Aug 2026); PLN Batam signed a 511 MVA supply deal with DayOne in Apr 2026.

Qualitative: EGAT plans 2027 transmission upgrades for eastern-region data centres; proposed rules would make developers reach commercial operation within 5 to 7 years or lose allocated capacity. No months-to-power figure.
JLL: average wait for a grid connection in primary data centre markets exceeds four years.
Ember: new facilities wait an average of seven to ten years, up to 13, in some primary markets.
source_name: Ember, Grids for data centres in Europe, 19 Jun 2025
